scenes.title: Scam calls
scenes.caption: Criminals are pretending to be your bank.
scenes.say: Your bank has noticed a rise in phone scams. Criminals ring up, pretending to be from the fraud team.

scenes.title: How it works
scenes.caption: A call, text or email says your account is at risk.
scenes.say: It might be a call, a text or an email. They say your account is at risk, and they may know your name and address.

scenes.title: The trick
scenes.caption: They say: move your money to a safe account.
scenes.say: Then comes the trick. They tell you to move your money to a safe account straight away. Even the number on your screen can look genuine.

scenes.title: Never
scenes.caption: Your bank will never ask for these things.
scenes.say: Your bank will never ask you to move money to a safe account. Nor for your full PIN, or your online password.

picture.heading: BANK WILL NEVER
items: Ask you to use a safe account
Ask you to read out a code

scenes.title: Hang up
scenes.caption: Hang up. Do not trust the number on your screen.
scenes.say: If a call like that comes, hang up. Wait five minutes, or use a different phone. Then ring the number on the back of your card.

scenes.title: Act fast
scenes.caption: Given details or moved money? Call at once, or ring 159.
scenes.say: If you think you have given details away or moved money, call your bank at once. You can also ring one five nine.

scenes.title: Remember
scenes.caption: A real bank will never rush you. It is fine to say no.
scenes.say: And remember this. A real bank will never rush you. Take your time. It is perfectly fine to say no.
